bug_report_content:
Title: Ar doesn't delete correct
Type: Bug | Priority: Major | Status: Resolved | Resolution: Fixed

Description:
When working on the Testcases i figured out that a deletion from an Ar Archive is not as successful as it look at first glance.
For example: my bla.ar file contains test1.xml and test2.xml. I delete test2.xml

The "getNextEntry" Method just delivers test1.xml. Looks correct.

But checking the result file at commandline brings the following:

$> ar -t /tmp/dir26673/bla.ar
test1.xml
test2.xml

vi shows me that there is still the test2.xml entry in the archive,
even when getNextEntry returns null.

Deleting test2.xml and adding test.txt afterward brings the following:

$> ar -t /tmp/dir24825/bla.ar
test.txt
ar: /tmp/dir24825/bla.ar: Inappropriate file type or format

Comments:

[Torsten Curdt]: Problem is that with

{code}
aos.putArchiveEntry(entry);
IOUtils.copy(ais, aos);
aos.closeArchiveEntry();
{code}

the copy does not stop at the entry boundary. So the above also copies other entries.

[Sebb]: Just to expand on the previous comment: 

The problem is that the ArArchiveInputStream does not break the stream into chunks - the read() methods should report EOF for each entry; getNextEntry() then allows read() to continue to the end of the new entry.

BTW, all three read() methods update the "offset" variable - it looks like this is a mistake.

[Christian Grobmeier]: Here is a patch which respects the chunks.
Its not perfect, but the Ar-Testcase runs. However, there is still an error in ChangeSetTestCase, but this can happen due to a TestCase problem.

I will apply this when I have my account. Please have a review here

Cheers,

[Sebb]: The method public int read(byte b[]) could now be deleted, as it now just does what the parent method does.

The method read() does not do any checking for end of entry; probably best to replace it with a call to read(byte[] b, int off, int len);
